entries.title: code_* adapters convert connect failures into offline results; only getProvider still throws
entries.summary: Both code-intelligence adapters catch connect/dead-client errors at their single guarded entry point and return a structured offline result, so the only throwing site on the code_* side is getProvider's unconfigured-provider-key resolution.

entries.title: Test no-injection branches by stripping process.env, never by injecting a real-passthrough deps function
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's filesystem quick-check is gated on if (!deps.execFileSync), so any deps injection -- even a wrapper that still shells out for real with no canned output -- skips that branch entirely and makes assertions about it unfalsifiable.

entries.title: kb_export and kb_import validate repo_path on the real filesystem before getKbProviders
entries.summary: In the table-driven forwarding test, kb_export and kb_import cannot use an arbitrary fake repo_path string like the other kb tools -- both resolve and validate the path against the real filesystem before the mocked getKbProviders is reached, so their table entries must anchor on real tmpdir fixtures.

entries.title: OS-assigned ephemeral ports can collide with undici's fetch blocked-port list, especially on hosts with a low dynamic port range
entries.summary: A server using listen(0) can still get a port on undici's WHATWG-fetch blocked-port list; fix is to detect a blocked bound port in listenOnPort and close-and-relisten, not to read the port earlier.

entries.title: zod-to-json-schema's jsonSchema2020-12 target is worse than its jsonSchema7 target
entries.summary: In zod-to-json-schema@3.25.1, target 'jsonSchema2020-12' differs from 'jsonSchema7' in exactly two ways and both are wrong for a real 2020-12 consumer: it emits no $schema at all, and it rewrites exclusive numeric bounds into the draft-04 boolean form that the 2020-12 metaschema rejects.

entries.title: One anchor policy, three branches: verbatim for read tools, hard-fail for kb_export
entries.summary: kb_session_prime and kb_stats pass a supplied repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim so an unreachable remote anchor stays honestly missing; kb_export deliberately keeps throwing instead, because it writes into repo_path -- and it throws before getKbProviders, so it never anchors at the server cwd either.

entries.title: Provider abstraction: never assume Claude
entries.summary: apra-fleet supports seven LLM providers (claude, agy, opencode, codex, copilot, gemini, none), not just Claude. Any auth/credential/dispatch-related change must go through the generic ProviderAdapter interface rather than assuming Claude-specific fields or behavior.

entries.title: check-sandbox-sync-remote.test.ts fails only when ambient BEADS_DIR is set
entries.summary: The embeddeddolt-layout case at tests/check-sandbox-sync-remote.test.ts:435 fails on any host with BEADS_DIR exported, because the bd child inherits it and resolves it before cwd; clearing BEADS_DIR makes all 55 tests pass.

entries.title: KB provider cache is now keyed by (slug, repoPath), not slug alone
entries.summary: getKbProviders/_providers Map keys on providerKey(slug, repoPath) via a NUL join, so two callers resolving to the same project slug but different repoPath values get distinct provider instances, each anchored at its own caller's repoPath.

entries.title: contract:generate projects 21 of taxonomy.json's 23 codes and emits openapi.yaml as JSON
entries.summary: Silent-surfaced codes are filtered out of both wire projections per taxonomy _meta.projection_rule, and bindings/openapi/openapi.yaml is JSON text with a .yaml extension so it stays on the same deterministic emit path.

entries.title: QueryOptions declares symbols, source_files and tags that no provider query() reads
entries.summary: Three QueryOptions fields are dead request surface: neither SqliteProvider.query nor HttpKbProvider.query reads opts.symbols, opts.source_files or opts.tags, and kbQuerySchema does not expose them.

entries.title: The round-trip harness asserts refusals by normalised message equality, not by taxonomy code
entries.summary: Taxonomy codes never appear on the wire, so the exit-criterion harness compares each refusal's live error message (after path/URL/id normalisation) byte-for-byte against the recorded message; any second provider adapter must reproduce those messages.

entries.title: Guard automated beads-export commits by comparing id sets, not file size or line count
entries.summary: A divergent local Dolt DB export can grow in total lines while dropping most previously-committed ids; the export-shrink-guard.mjs guard compares id sets to catch this, mirroring kb_export's shrink precedent.

entries.title: A directory-level gitignore rule shadows everything inside it, un-ignore patterns included
entries.summary: The blanket '/sprint-logs/' rule made every file under sprint-logs unstageable regardless of narrower rules elsewhere; only removing the directory rule and keeping the scoped '**/sprint-logs/sprint_*.json' rule restored the durable-vs-scratch split the sprint workflow documents.

entries.title: bd dolt remote list --json prints null, not [], when no remotes are configured
entries.summary: parseDoltRemoteList must map the JSON literal null to an empty array; treating null as an unexpected shape makes checkDoltRemoteAbsent return ok:false ('could not parse') for a repo that is simply not wired to any Dolt remote.

entries.title: Local members use host OAuth; provision_llm_auth skips them
entries.summary: Local fleet members share the orchestrator's own machine, so they use whatever OAuth session is already active on that host. provision_llm_auth explicitly skips local members rather than attempting to provision credentials for them.

entries.title: The nonexistent-path + NO-url slug assertion passes on both pre-fix and post-fix trees
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(<nonexistent windows path>) returning 'default' is NOT a pre-fix failure and cannot be used as a regression pin for the remote-URL work; the assertions that actually go red on the pre-fix tree are the URL-bearing ones.

entries.title: No kb_* tool reads SqliteProvider.repoPath; the sweep root defaults inside the provider
entries.summary: kb_freshness_sweep calls freshnessSweep() with no argument, so the sweep root is resolved from the provider's own repoPath field rather than passed in by the tool layer.

entries.title: kb-remote-scope.test.ts pins handler forwarding, not the zod schema spread
entries.summary: The b4g.1.5 end-to-end test calls kbCapture/kbList with raw objects cast 'as any', so it bypasses zod parse entirely and cannot detect a dropped ...kbScopeFields spread; that layer is pinned only by kb-remote-url-forwarding.test.ts.

entries.title: kb_capture.role is an open string on purpose; the Author enum is handler-enforced
entries.summary: Any generated schema or binding will show kb_capture.role as a bare {"type":"string"} with no enum. That is deliberate: AUTHOR_VALUES/validateAuthor in the handler stamps 'unknown' for anything outside the Author list, so an invalid role hint degrades instead of rejecting the whole capture call.

entries.title: repo_remote_url is defined once in kbScopeFields but only 3 of ~16 kb_* tools spread it
entries.summary: src/services/knowledge/kb-scope-input.ts holds the single zod definition; only kb_session_prime, kb_capture and kb_harvest spread it, so kb_list and the other read tools silently drop the field and resolve to the path-derived KB.

entries.title: memory-contract error refs are positional JSON Pointers, so reordering taxonomy.json silently rewrites published identifiers
entries.summary: taxonomyCodeRef() builds taxonomy.json#/groups/<group>/codes/<index> refs that carry no code string, and contract:check cannot detect a reorder because all three ref sets come from one loadProjectableCodes() call.

entries.title: The embeddeddolt sandbox test can pass vacuously when bd is unavailable
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's bd-unavailable fallback message contains the word 'unavailable', which the embeddeddolt test's own /Dolt-level remotes|unavailable/ assertion accepts -- so on a machine without bd the test is green without ever reaching the parser it is meant to exercise.

entries.title: Every kb_*/code_* tool response is a single un-annotated content block, never the 3-block wrapTool envelope
entries.summary: wrapTool can build up to three content blocks with annotations and structuredContent, but none of the 23 kb_*/code_* contract tools can reach that shape: the nudge fires only for register_member/execute_prompt, the preamble is suppressed for JSON payloads, and no kb_*/code_* handler returns structuredContent.

entries.title: methods.json now formally splits error_codes from taxonomy non_error_outcomes via a dedicated field
entries.summary: As of my-beads-db-27m.44, memory-contract/v1/methods.json's error_codes arrays no longer carry bare non-error names; affected methods (P-2, P-10, P-12, X-2, C-1..C-7) cite taxonomy.json non_error_outcomes names in a separate non_error_outcomes field instead, enforced by a new tests/memory-contract-taxonomy.test.ts assertion.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: memory-contract fixture corpus volatility is real and confirmed on three specific axes across two commits
entries.summary: memory-contract/v1/fixtures is not byte-reproducible: entry id (fresh UUID), created_at (wall-clock), and result order (kb_list/happy.json) all vary between recordings of the same scenario -- confirmed against real commits f230c530 and 8d6a5e00, and fixed for semantic comparison via normalizeVolatileFixtureFields in roundtrip-harness.mjs.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's plain npm test never sets APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se's "test" script runs node --test directly with --test-concurrency=8, but does NOT set the APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY env var -- only the separate test:unit/test:integration/test:record scripts (which route through scripts/run-tests.mjs) set it. A scaledTimeout()/waitFor() call that relies on the env var being set will silently use an unscaled timeout under plain npm test.

entries.title: Interpolating JSON.stringify(path) into an auto-sprint node -e command breaks the shell quoting
entries.summary: auto-sprint.js builds dispatched commands as node -e "..."; embedding a path with JSON.stringify inside that double-quoted string injects inner double quotes, so the shell strips them and node dies with a SyntaxError before any logic runs.

entries.title: Tests that spawn real subprocesses need per-test timeouts sized to subprocess cost, not the framework default
entries.summary: Tests spawning git clone, PowerShell, or an external CLI reliably pass in isolation but flake under full-suite parallel load purely from host contention; the durable fix is a per-test timeout sized to real subprocess cost, never a global bump or a skip.

entries.title: x-invariant annotations are T1.2.2's job, not the postprocess module's
entries.summary: GENERATOR-DECISION.md's INV-01..INV-09 table is a mapping deliverable only; no committed code stamps x-invariant onto emitted schemas, and postprocessTo2020_12 deliberately does not.

entries.title: auto-sprint workflow VM has no fs/os/process.env, so path redaction must be pure string work
entries.summary: redactHomeFromTranscriptDir anchors on the literal '/.claude/projects/' substring instead of comparing against $HOME because the auto-sprint workflow VM cannot read env or fs; the anchor is safe only because Setup Step 7 constructs transcriptDir as $HOME/.claude/projects/<slug>.

entries.title: git add <dir>/ errors on a directory-level ignore but silently no-ops on an inner file glob
entries.summary: The failure mode of an ignored sprint-logs/ is not uniform: a directory rule like '/sprint-logs/' makes `git add sprint-logs/` exit 1 with an explicit advice message, while a file-glob rule like '**/sprint-logs/*.jsonl' makes the same command exit 0 and stage nothing.

entries.title: agent.gitRepos is a bare owner/repo access-list, never a full git remote URL, in live fleet data
entries.summary: Empirically verified against this fleet's own ~/.apra-fleet/data/registry.json: every populated gitRepos entry across all registered members (local and remote) is a short 'Owner/Repo' GitHub identifier, never a scheme-qualified clone URL -- confirming src/services/vcs/github.ts's own https://github.com/${repo}.git construction (used only for connectivity testing) is the correct mental model for what this field actually contains.

entries.title: APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR overrides FLEET_DIR but not three hardcoded-homedir code-intelligence paths
entries.summary: Setting APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR redirects src/paths.ts's FLEET_DIR (and everything built on it: KB sqlite files, onboarding.json, knowledge/config.json), but code-intelligence.ts's provider CONFIG_PATH, code-intelligence-telemetry.ts's USAGE_DIR, and code-intelligence-codebase-memory.ts's CACHE_DIR all build their path from os.homedir() directly, bypassing the override entirely.

entries.title: {{secure.NAME}} substitution is pre-escaped and launch-time bound
entries.summary: execute_command resolves {{secure.NAME}} fleet-secret placeholders with single-quote escaping already applied. Reference the token bare in a command string, not wrapped in your own quotes -- double-escaping produces a corrupted value and a false 401/invalid-token error.

entries.title: The kb_/code_ tool response envelope is not always a single text block
entries.summary: wrapTool can prepend an extra annotated apra-fleet-display text block, so a response-schema generated as a one-element content array is wrong for the code_* tools whose payload stringifies to a scalar.

entries.title: bindings/openapi/openapi.yaml is JSON text under a .yaml name, by design
entries.summary: contract:generate emits openapi.yaml through the same JSON.stringify emit() path as the schemas, relying on JSON being valid YAML 1.2 flow; there is no YAML serializer or parser anywhere in the repo.

entries.title: Same-slug callers now open two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite
entries.summary: Keying the KB provider cache by (slug, repoPath) means two local clones of the same remote get two separate SqliteProvider instances pointed at the same kb.sqlite file; this is safe by design because init sets WAL plus busy_timeout=5000.

entries.title: Member OS resolution: always via agent.os
entries.summary: The orchestrator and each fleet member can independently run Windows/Mac/Linux -- local members share the orchestrator's own OS, but remote members can be any OS regardless of the orchestrator's. Never assume a target member's shell/OS matches the orchestrator's.

entries.title: kb-setup is the one kb tool that takes repo_path but resolves no KB
entries.summary: Fifteen of the sixteen src/tools/kb-*.ts tools spread kbScopeFields and forward repo_remote_url to getKbProviders; kb-setup is excluded by design because its repo_path only locates a .git dir for hook installation and it writes a single global config, never selecting a project KB.

entries.title: kb_session_prime must pass an explicit repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim, never through resolveRepoPath
entries.summary: Validating repo_path before handing it to getKbProviders converts a remote member's unreachable path into the fleet server's own cwd, silently staling healthy entries in the shared project KB; the anchor must stay honestly missing.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: The auto-sprint beads export can replace the committed id set, not just grow it
entries.summary: auto-sprint.js exports and stages .beads/issues.jsonl unguarded, so a sprint run whose Dolt DB diverges from the repo's committed export silently deletes issue records while the file grows in size.

entries.title: A missing-anchor freshness regression surfaces first as kb_list dropping entries, not as a stale-flag assertion
entries.summary: In tests/knowledge/kb-remote-member-e2e.test.ts the four remote-member assertions live in one it(), so removing SqliteProvider's anchorIsMissing guard fails at the SAME DATABASE read-back (line 165) and never reaches the raw stale-row check (line 181).

entries.title: LocalStrategy's rolling inactivity timer never resets for a command that emits no stdout/stderr, so timeoutMs becomes a total wall-clock ceiling, not an idle-detection window
entries.summary: resetInactivityTimer only fires from stdout/stderr 'data' handlers, so any silent command (mkdir, a file write, a cat/Get-Content against a missing file) gets no resets at all -- for those callers timeoutMs is effectively a hard ceiling on spawn+run, not real inactivity detection, and must be sized for host-contention scheduling delay, not command runtime.

entries.title: Recorded wrapTool envelopes omit parsed, so kb_* round-trip fixtures fail their own response schemas
entries.summary: memory-contract/v1/fixtures records the raw {content} envelope, but the published kb_* response schemas require parsed, so 25 of 32 recorded responses are invalid against the very schemas the corpus exists to validate.

entries.title: openapi.yaml is JSON-shaped YAML emitted through emit(), and tests rely on that
entries.summary: memory-contract/v1/bindings/openapi/openapi.yaml is written by the same JSON.stringify-based emit() helper, so it is valid JSON as well as YAML -- which is why the parity test JSON.parses a .yaml file.

entries.title: Published response schemas are narrower than the real wrapTool envelope
entries.summary: The emitted *.response.json files pin content to exactly one un-annotated block with a closed root, but wrapTool can return three blocks, annotations, and structuredContent.

entries.title: The embeddeddolt test now branches on bd availability instead of a loose regex
entries.summary: tests/check-sandbox-sync-remote.test.ts probes `bd --version` and asserts /Dolt-level remotes/ when bd is reachable, /unavailable/ when it is not, closing the vacuous-pass hole the old combined regex left open.

entries.title: zod's native toJSONSchema cannot read this repo's v3-authored tool schemas
entries.summary: zod 3.25.76 ships the v4 API at the zod/v4 subpath including z.toJSONSchema, but that emitter only walks v4 internals, so it throws TypeError reading 'def' on any schema authored with the v3 import - which is every schema in src/tools/.

entries.title: taxonomy.json quarantines directive activation by absence, not by a refusal code
entries.summary: The v1 error taxonomy holds the three CLI-only directive approve/reject error codes in excluded_from_closed_set outside every group, while still publishing the governance refusals of activation attempts made on routes that really exist.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: Four resolveRepoPath helpers exist in src/tools, but only prime and stats ever had the null-to-cwd shape
entries.summary: kb-session-prime.ts and kb-stats.ts returned string|null and degraded to process.cwd(); kb-export.ts and kb-import.ts have always returned string and thrown, so they were never part of the b4g.7 anchor defect despite the bead naming kb-export as a third instance.

entries.title: The .trim() guard in resolveProjectSlug is provably redundant and cannot be pinned by any test
entries.summary: project-slug.ts guards its remote-URL short-circuit twice, but the outer remoteUrl.trim() check is unreachable-by-effect given slugify, so no input can distinguish its removal and no regression test can pin it.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: contract:generate reads dist, not src, and is byte-idempotent
entries.summary: memory-contract/v1/generate-contract.mjs imports the compiled dist/tools/*.js schemas, so npm run build must precede npm run contract:generate; re-running it leaves git status empty.

entries.title: git check-ignore silently skips tracked paths unless --no-index
entries.summary: An acceptance criterion of the form 'git check-ignore -v <path> returns no match' does not prove the path is unignored -- check-ignore ignores index entries by default, so any tracked path reports no match even when a .gitignore rule matches it.

entries.title: postprocess definitions rename is container-aware via a JSON-Pointer state machine
entries.summary: normaliseSchemaMap keeps map KEYS untouched and rewriteDefinitionsPointer walks pointer segments in schema/mapName states, so a user field or $defs entry literally named definitions survives.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: MemoryProvider implementations diverge outside the shared interface (teardown name, capture signature)
entries.summary: SqliteProvider and HttpKbProvider both implement MemoryProvider but differ in teardown method name and in capture's parameter list, breaking polymorphic binding generation.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: apra-pm test suite is deliberately not an npm workspace, so local npm test must invoke it via explicit --prefix
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm is excluded from the root npm workspaces array on purpose (to avoid lockfile churn), so its suite is only reachable via an explicit --prefix invocation -- both CI and the local run-all-tests.mjs must include that invocation or local runs give false green signals.

entries.title: The kb_/code_ MCP surface is 23 tools, and none of them declares a response schema
entries.summary: registerAllTools registers exactly 16 kb_* and 7 code_* tools (23 of 57 total), every one with a request shape only -- no response zod schema and no structuredContent anywhere in that surface, because all 23 handlers return a bare JSON-stringified string through wrapTool.

entries.title: A low TCP dynamic port range makes listen(0) hand back fetch-blocked ports
entries.summary: On a host whose TCP dynamic port range starts at 1024, server.listen(0) can bind one of the WHATWG fetch blocked ports, so any Node fetch()-based client fails with 'bad port' -- looking exactly like a load-dependent test flake.

entries.title: An unmatched kb_capture supersedes request is silently ignored, not rejected
entries.summary: makeAudnDecision honours supersedes:<id> only if that candidate independently passes the dedup gates (same type, symbol overlap, file overlap, target not an ACTIVE directive); otherwise the request falls through to the ordinary AUDN paths with no error, so the caller believes it retired an entry that is still live.

entries.title: deploy.md's Permissions section is the source of truth for .claude/settings.json allow-list
entries.summary: The deploy phase's runnable command set is defined by deploy.md lines 6-18, and .claude/settings.json permissions.allow must mirror exactly that list -- bead descriptions quoting an older list are stale and must not be followed.

entries.title: contract:generate --check cannot see a newly registered tool, only a deleted one
entries.summary: The generator's roster is the hardcoded KB_MODULES/CODE_EXPORTS list with EXPECTED_TOOL_COUNT = 23 and no import of the live tool registry, so --check catches deletions and strays but never a tool newly registered in tool-registry.ts.

entries.title: Only fix 1 of postprocess-2020-12 fires on the real 23-tool surface
entries.summary: Emitting all 23 inventoried request schemas with the chosen jsonSchema7 + definitionPath $defs config produces no definitions key, no boolean exclusive bound and no array-form items, so only the dialect fix is reachable there.

entries.title: HttpKbProvider falls back to local only on connection errors, not on HTTP 4xx/5xx or bad JSON
entries.summary: isConnectionError matches only ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND/ETIMEDOUT/ECONNRESET/socket-hang-up, so a remote 500 or a malformed remote body propagates as a throw instead of degrading to the SqliteProvider fallback.

entries.title: HttpKbProvider.sync mirrors stats E-STATS-UNSUPPORTED pattern, not a throw
entries.summary: HttpKbProvider.sync() hardcodes return {synced:false, reason:'local-only provider'} regardless of opts, same non-throwing documented-not-supported shape as stats' E-STATS-UNSUPPORTED, so both belong in the same verdict class for contract-binding purposes.

entries.title: The auto-sprint cost ledger is staged by an unconditional plain git add sprint-logs/
entries.summary: beads-export-cleanup stages sprint logs with a plain, unguarded `git add sprint-logs/` before `bd export` and the export commit, pinned by sprint-log-flush.test.mjs -- so any gitignore rule covering that directory silently drops the ledger rather than erroring.

entries.title: The memory-contract drift guard needs both halves: CI git-diff cannot see untracked emitted files
entries.summary: The CI regenerate-and-diff step uses git diff --exit-code, which ignores untracked files, so a newly emitted uncommitted artifact passes that step; the vitest --check half is what reports MISSING/EXTRA.

entries.title: Injecting deps.execFileSync into checkDoltRemoteAbsent silently disables its filesystem probe
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent guards its whole .beads layout quick-check with if (!deps.execFileSync), so any test that injects deps to control the child env stops testing layout recognition and its no-short-circuit assertion becomes unfalsifiable.

entries.title: bd prints literal 'null' for an empty dolt remote list, not an empty array
entries.summary: Code parsing bd's dolt-remote-list output must treat a parsed result of null (or whitespace-padded 'null\n') as 'no remotes configured' rather than a parse error; any other non-array non-null shape is still a genuine error.

entries.title: gitRepos is single-entry-safe, multi-entry-ambiguous for deriving an origin URL
entries.summary: knownRepoRemoteUrl(agent) in src/tools/execute-prompt.ts only treats agent.gitRepos[0] as a genuine origin URL when gitRepos has exactly one entry; a multi-entry gitRepos (an access list, not an origin field) is left unforwarded even if its first element already looks like a URL, since it could belong to an unrelated repo.

entries.title: Fixture expected_error_code and observed_via mean different things and only one is cross-checked
entries.summary: In the recorded corpus, expected_error_code asserts the fixture's own tool raises that taxonomy code; observed_via records that the response is downstream evidence of a code another tool raised, and must not be cross-checked against the tool's bindings.

entries.title: Six SqliteProvider methods are tool-reachable but absent from the MemoryProvider interface
entries.summary: MemoryProvider (types.ts:230) declares 12 methods, but registered kb_* tools additionally call list, feedback, freshnessSweep, resolveContradiction, reconcilePrefilter and hasEntry plus the repoPath property directly on SqliteProvider -- so code typed against the interface alone does not cover the real surface.

entries.title: memory-contract v1 response schemas now declare parsed optional, not required
entries.summary: response-schemas.mjs's responseSchema() used to require both content and parsed on every kb_*/code_* response schema, but no wrapTool handler ever puts a literal parsed key on the wire -- it was made optional (my-beads-db-27m.47) so raw recorded envelopes validate as-is while still fully typing the parsed body when a consumer decodes it.

entries.title: contract:generate --check does not enumerate registered tools; it trusts the hardcoded roster
entries.summary: The --check parity mode of memory-contract/v1/generate-contract.mjs compares generated documents against committed ones using KB_MODULES/CODE_EXPORTS resolved against dist/tools, so a tool registered in tool-registry.ts but missing from that roster still passes check.

entries.title: HttpKbProvider.query drops ids, so kb_query L2 hydration would return wrong rows over HTTP
entries.summary: The HTTP provider forwards only query/type/limit/l1_only/include_stale/include_superseded, so query({ids}) becomes a parameter-less remote GET while SqliteProvider treats ids as an exact-id fetch.
